controls.label: Scaling 1/sqrt(d_k)
controls.help: When on, scores are divided by sqrt(d_k); when off, raw dot products are used, so weights can become sharper.

visuals.title: Weighted output per query and value dimension

explorations.title: Equal scores give uniform weights
explorations.instruction: Predict: when both keys produce the same score for a query, what will the attention weights look like? Then apply the preset, which sets q, k, v, and scaling.
explorations.observe: Both rows of weights become 0.50 and 0.50, and the output rows become the average of the value rows, 1 and 1.
explorations.why: Identical scores give identical exponentials, so softmax divides each by the same total and returns uniform weights. The output then averages the value rows.

explorations.title: Dominant score without scaling
explorations.instruction: Predict: when one key has a much larger raw dot product than the other, how concentrated will the weights be? Then apply the preset, which sets q, k, v, and turns scaling off.
explorations.observe: The first row of weights puts most mass on the first key, while the second row stays near 0.50 and 0.50 because its query is zero. The first output row pulls toward the first value row.
explorations.why: Turning scaling off keeps the raw score 3, so the softmax exponentiates 3 against 0 and strongly favors the larger score. Scaling would divide the score by sqrt(2) and soften the peak.

invariants.name: weights stay between zero and one
